sources.title: Constitution of Tonga, 2020 Revised Edition
sources.publisher: Attorney General's Office, Tonga

claims.text: Clauses 30 and 41 describe a constitutional monarchy; royal signature is required for legislation. Clause 36 assigns military command to the King but requires Assembly consent for war.

The King appoints the Assembly-recommended elected representative as prime minister. Cabinet exercises executive authority collectively and answers to the Assembly; ministers are nominated by the prime minister and appointed by the King. Reserved royal powers are excluded.
The King appoints Privy Council advisers. The Council also handles specified hereditary estate and title appeals.
The Assembly includes nobles' representatives, people's representatives and Cabinet. Its recommended Speaker must be an elected nobles' representative and is appointed by the King.

Clause 32 of the 2020 Revised Edition sets hereditary succession to the Crown and Throne: to the eldest male child and the heirs of his body, through the male line, then to the female line, with fallback procedures if there is no lawful heir.
claims.uncertainty: A legal rule in a consolidated edition. It dates no accession and is not backdated to 1990. Re-read on 2026-09-21 for CLAUDE-C01-07; the source's recorded access date is that of its first intake. Downloaded copy: 789,048 bytes, SHA-256 197f1dcaf64c3267e589354aafdc2783dae7fac9f4d3b296808d21d45f7004de.

claims.text: Clause 34 prescribes the oath to be taken by those who succeed to the throne. The clause does not make succession conditional on the oath, and it does not fix when the oath is taken.
claims.uncertainty: No coronation-oath event is dated by this clause, and no retrieved source dates the oath for George Tupou V or Tupou VI. Re-read on 2026-09-21 for CLAUDE-C01-07; the source's recorded access date is that of its first intake.

claims.text: Clause 43 provides: 'Should the King wish to travel abroad it shall be lawful for him to appoint a Prince Regent who shall administer the affairs of the Kingdom during his absence.' If the King dies while his heir is under eighteen and his will names no Prince Regent, the Legislative Assembly 'shall choose by ballot a Prince Regent', 'but the representatives of the people shall have no voice in such election'. Clause 42 refers a minority regency to clause 43.
claims.uncertainty: Enabling provision only; it records no appointment. A regent administers the Kingdom during the King's absence or the heir's minority and is not a King. Re-read on 2026-09-21 for CLAUDE-C01-07; the source's recorded access date is that of its first intake.

sources.scope_note: Consolidated edition, not a complete amendment or commencement ledger. Do not backdate these provisions to 1990 or assume no later amendments.

sources.publisher: Legislative Assembly of Tonga

claims.text: The minutes of sitting No. 48 (Monday 9 December 2024), whose agenda listed Motion No. 4A/2024 for a vote of no confidence in the Prime Minister and the Prime Minister's written reply, record Prime Minister Siaosi Sovaleni ('Eiki Palēmia) announcing in the House, under the heading 'Fakafisi 'Eiki Palēmia mei he lakanga Palēmia 'o Tonga', that he resigns as Prime Minister of Tonga 'Fakatatau ki he Konisitūtoné Kupu 50 (2)(c), effective immediately he 'ahó ni' (in accordance with clause 50(2)(c), effective immediately today), and taking leave of the Deputy Prime Minister and Cabinet.
claims.locator: PDF p.3 (agenda items 4.1-4.2); PDF pp.40-41 (heading; time blocks 1150-1155 and 1155-1200)
claims.uncertainty: The clause is printed '50 (2)(c)'; the Speaker later cites clause 50(a)(2)(c). The printed form is kept and not corrected. The time of day is bracketed only by the transcript's five-minute blocks. The resignation letter itself, and the date on which it was written or signed, are not in the minutes. The Speaker relied on His Majesty's written reply, not on these words, for confirmation (to_speaker_vonc_withdrawn_procedure_20241209).

claims.text: The same minutes record the Table Clerk reading, in the 1400-1405 block after the House resumed, a letter from the Palace Office dated Monday 9 December 2024, signed by Sione U. Fifita, Secretary to His Majesty, and addressed to Speaker Lord Fakafanua: the Palace Office had received that day, Monday 9 December 2024, Hon. Hu'akavameiliku's letter to King Tupou VI resigning as Prime Minister of Tonga, and His Majesty had graciously accepted the resignation ('Kuo mokoi 'a e Finangalo 'a 'Ene 'Afio ki he fakafisi').
claims.locator: PDF p.42: Speaker's adjournment to 2pm at the top of the page; 1400-1405 block, heading 'Tohi mei he 'Ofisi Palasi fekau'aki mo e Tohi Fakafisi Palēmia 'o Tonga'
claims.uncertainty: The Palace letter is known only as read into the minutes; the original and the resignation letter are not published. The minutes bracket the acceptance: the resignation was announced in the 1150-1200 block; the Speaker then said the matter was to be completed with His Majesty under the Constitution and adjourned the House to 2pm; at 1400-1405 he said the recess had been used to convey it to His Majesty ('Na'a tau ngāue'aki aipē 'a e taimi mālōlō ke fakahoko eni ki he 'Ene 'Afio') and that the Palace letter had then reached his Office. Acceptance therefore fell within that recess on 9 December; its clock time is not recorded.

claims.text: The Speaker then removed agenda items 4.1 and 4.2 (the no-confidence motion and the Prime Minister's reply), ruled that both documents be released as public records of the Assembly although not tabled, and stated that because the office of Prime Minister was vacant the Schedule under clause 50(A) applied: invitations within 10 days, counted from the next day; 14 days for nominations, expected to end on Monday 23 December; and a meeting within 3 days, to be held on 24 December, to which he adjourned the House. He also read clause 50(a)(2)(c) (a Prime Minister holds office until death, resignation or revocation of appointment) and stated that the resignation had been confirmed that day by His Majesty's written reply ('tohi tali mei he 'Ene 'Afió').
claims.locator: PDF p.43 (end of the 1400-1405 block: items 4.1-4.2 removed and public-record ruling; 1405-1410 block: the Schedule); p.46 (1410-1415: clause 50(a)(2)(c) read; 1415-1420: confirmation by His Majesty's reply); p.50 (adjournment to 24 Tīsema)
claims.uncertainty: Procedural statements by the Speaker in debate. No vote on the motion took place; this is a clause 50A vacancy, not a clause 50B removal.

claims.text: Answering Lord Tu'ivakanō's request that the King be asked for an interim Cabinet ('Kapineti fakataimi') during the 14-day period, the Speaker had section 18(2) of the Government Act read (the Deputy Prime Minister exercises the powers and performs the duties of the Prime Minister when the Prime Minister cannot act because of absence, illness or other reason) and ruled that on a resignation under clause 50(a) the existing Cabinet remains and, under the Government Act, the Deputy Prime Minister acts ('Le'ole'o leva 'a e 'Eiki Tokoni Palēmiá'); he found no constitutional power for the King to remove the Cabinet short of dissolving the Assembly, the Cabinet leaving office under the Constitution only when the Prime Minister is removed under clause 50(b).
claims.locator: PDF pp.47-50 (headings 'Tokanga Nōpele Tongatapu 2 ke 'omai ha Kapineti Fakataimi ...'; 1420-1430 blocks)
claims.uncertainty: The Speaker's ruling in debate, not an instrument appointing an Acting Prime Minister. It names no person and dates no start. The Government Act was not retrieved; section 18(2) is taken only as read into the minutes. Ha'apai 13 cites an earlier precedent of a Prime Minister's death, which is not imported.

Siaosi Sovaleni against ''Eiki Palēmia' with Education & Training and Police & Fire Services, and Hon. Tiofilusi Tiueti against Finance & National Planning and Revenue & Customs. sources.publisher: Attorney General's Office, Tonga (Tonga Law Reports; judgments of the Supreme Court and Court of Appeal)

claims.text: In Pohiva v Lasike (Supreme Court, Hampton CJ, Cr App 95/96, judgment 1 August 1997) the court records that during a sitting of the Legislative Assembly on 2nd August 1995 the appellant, a people's representative, was interrupted in debate by 'the Acting Speaker, the Honourable Lasike' and threw a volume of the Laws of Tonga that hit him; the Assembly suspended the appellant for 14 days and the Acting Speaker brought a private prosecution for assault.
claims.locator: [1997] Tonga LR 247-248 (PDF pages 135-136): headnote; judgment lines 50-81
claims.uncertainty: Acting Speaker presiding on one sitting day: a claim only, never a holder. The source names him only by his noble title, and no identity with the Lord Lasike of 2010-2012 is asserted. The judgment does not say who appointed him, for how long, or who the substantive Speaker was. The 1996 volume's report of Moala v Minister of Police places the incident 'in October 1995' with 'the then Acting or Deputy Speaker' (a lead, listed in the report); the dated appellate account is used and the conflict is retained.

claims.text: In 'Akau'ola v Attorney General (Court of Appeal, Morling, Burchett and Tompkins JJ, App. 3/97, 12 and 20 June 1997) the court states that on 14 November 1996 the appellant journalist 'interviewed the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly' about the Chief Justice's order of 14 October 1996 releasing three persons imprisoned under a warrant issued by the Speaker; the article it quotes begins 'In a statement by Fusitu'a [i.e. the Speaker]'.
claims.locator: [1997] Tonga LR 36-37 (PDF page 30): header; judgment lines 55-80
claims.uncertainty: Shows who held the office on 14 November 1996 only; no appointment, start or end date. The source names him only by his noble title (Fusitu'a); the gloss '[i.e. the Speaker]' is the court's. The contempt proceedings are not imported.

claims.text: In Attorney General v Fusitu'a, 'Akau'ola & Moala (Supreme Court, Lewis J, C.1329/96, 12 December 1996, January and 4 February 1997) the judge finds that Fusitu'a spoke the published words in the interview of 14 November 1996 and that 'Fusitu'a was at all material times the Speaker of the Supreme Law making Body of Tonga' [the Legislative Assembly]; he adds that the reversal of the will of Parliament 'would not be tolerated while he was Speaker' and, on sentence, that 'For years he has carried well, the solemn burden in his role as Speaker'.
claims.locator: [1997] Tonga LR 18-31 (PDF pages 21-27): header and headnote pp. 18-19; the interview finding p. 26 (PDF page 25); p. 30 lines 581-587 and p. 31 lines 646-650 (PDF page 27)
claims.uncertainty: 'For years' gives no start year. The source names him only by his noble title; the bracketed gloss is this packet's. The court held that he spoke in a personal capacity; the contempt finding and penalty are not imported.

sources.title: Act of Constitution of Tonga (Amendment) (No. 2) Act 2010, Act No. 20 of 2010 (AGO amending-legislation copy)

claims.text: Section 19 replaces clause 61 of the Constitution: 'The King shall, within 5 days after the appointment of a Prime Minister in accordance with clause 50A following a general election, appoint one of the elected representatives of the nobles on the recommendation of the Legislative Assembly, to be the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.'
claims.uncertainty: Procedure only. The Act dates no Speaker's selection, appointment or oath, and prints no commencement provision. It is not backdated before the 2010 reform and not read as the procedure in force at any later date without a consolidation check.

claims.text: New clause 61(2)-(4): the Speaker remains in office until the King appoints an Interim Speaker following the next general election under sub-section (8) of the Schedule, until his appointment is revoked under sub-clause (3), or until he dies, resigns or his appointment is revoked after he ceases to be an elected representative of the nobles for any reason other than the dissolution of the Assembly; on the Prime Minister's recommendation with the approval of at least half of the members the King revokes the Speaker's appointment and appoints a new Speaker on the Assembly's recommendation; and the King appoints a Speaker within 7 days of a vacancy.
claims.locator: Section 19, new clause 61(2), (3) and (4), PDF page 12
claims.uncertainty: Procedure only. It is never used to date the end of any Speaker's tenure (for example from a later Interim Speaker's appointment) or to fill a vacancy date.

claims.text: The inserted Schedule (clause 50A) requires the King, within 7 days of the declaration of the result of a general election, to appoint a person who was not a candidate as Interim Speaker, who holds office 'until a Speaker is next appointed under clause 61'; the Interim Speaker invites and receives the nominations for Prime Minister Designate and convenes the ballot, and in any other vacancy in the office of Prime Minister, except after a vote of no confidence, 'the Speaker shall perform the role of the Interim Speaker'.
claims.uncertainty: Procedure only. An Interim Speaker is not a Speaker holder, and no interim appointment is dated by this text.

roles.title: King

holder_claims.name: Taufa'ahau Tupou IV
holder_claims.note: King when the period opens: dated royal assents of 12 July and 8 August 1990 (TO-CROWN-01). His reign ended with his death in Auckland at 00:34 on 11 September 2006, Tongan time (23:34 on 10 September, New Zealand time), as Gazette No. 20 records; Gazette No. 19 states that the Crown devolved by his decease (TO-CROWN-03, TO-CROWN-04).
holder_claims.uncertainty: The start of the reign (1965) is outside the period and is not structured. The end is the Tongan calendar date of the death, to which the proclamation's devolution wording ties the transfer of the Crown; it is not taken from George Tupou V's proclamation or coronation. The State Funeral, burial and mourning are separate claims.

holder_claims.name: George Tupou V
holder_claims.note: Formerly Crown Prince Tupouto'a; Siaosi Tupou V in the Tongan texts. Accession by devolution of the Crown on the decease of Taufa'ahau Tupou IV at 00:34 on 11 September 2006, Tongan time (TO-CROWN-04); proclaimed King by Gazette No. 19 on the same Tongan day, as a separate event. Traditional installation (taumafa kava) on 30 July 2008 and coronation on 1 August 2008 (TO-CROWN-05). Died in Hong Kong at 20:58 on 18 March 2012, Tonga time (TO-CROWN-06).
holder_claims.uncertainty: The start is the stated devolution on his predecessor's death, not the proclamation, the traditional installation, the coronation or the coronation oath (which no source dates). The end is his death as Gazette Extraordinary No. 8 records it; Gazette Extraordinary No. 9 states that the Crown devolved by his decease. No accession time is stored.

holder_claims.name: Tupou VI
holder_claims.note: Formerly Crown Prince Tupouto'a Lavaka, the former Prince 'Ulukalala Lavaka Ata, on whom the Crown Prince title was vested in September 2006. Accession by devolution of the Crown on the decease of George Tupou V at 20:58 on 18 March 2012, Tonga time; proclaimed King on 19 March 2012 as a separate event (TO-CROWN-07); crowned on 4 July 2015 (TO-CROWN-08).
holder_claims.uncertainty: The start is the stated devolution on his predecessor's death, not the proclamation or the coronation. No end is inferred: no source here records one before the 7 September 2026 cutoff, and the latest attestation in this packet is 18 December 2025 (to_tupou_vi_2025).

roles.scope_note: Holder observations carry from/until only where a source states them: accession by devolution of the Crown on the predecessor's death, as each proclamation states, and death. Proclamations, the traditional installation, coronations and the coronation oath are separate claims and never a start date. Prince or Princess Regent observations are claims on to_crown, not reigns or to_king holders.

holder_claims.note: Deputy Prime Minister, Attorney General and Minister of Justice from the royal consent in Privy Council 'with effect from 24th January, 2001' until his resignation at 4 p.m. on 28 September 2001, accepted that day by the Princess Regent (TO-DPM-03). holder_claims.name: Samiu Kuita Vaipulu

holder_claims.uncertainty: The start is the stated day the Cabinet ministers commenced; the report of 3 January 2011 is not a start. No end is stated: CLAUDE-C01-08's styling of him as 'caretaker Deputy Prime Minister' on 29 December 2014 is not cited, and no end is inferred from the Cabinet effective 31 December 2014. His acting premierships are claims on to_pm.

holder_claims.name: Siaosi Sovaleni
holder_claims.note: Listed as Deputy Prime Minister in the Pohiva Cabinet announced on 31 December 2014; attested to 30 August 2017 (TO-DPM-07). A separate observation from the to_pm holder "Siaosi 'Ofakivahafolau Sovaleni" of 2021-2024.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No from: the release states only the Prime Minister-elect's recommendation and that the appointments 'will be effective as of 31st December, 2014' (to_dpm_sovaleni_appointment_recommended_20141231), and IPU's Cabinet date of 19 January 2015 conflicts. No until: the PMO states only that the Prime Minister recommended the revocation 'effective from 1st September, 2017' (to_dpm_sovaleni_revocation_recommended_20170901), and the royal endorsement it reports covers the new appointments; Lord Ma'afu's start is not used as an end.

holder_claims.name: Lord Ma'afu
holder_claims.note: Appointed Deputy Prime Minister by the King's endorsement under the Royal Sign Manual 'with effect from 1st September, 2017', conveyed to the PMO on 5 September 2017 (TO-DPM-08).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No later attestation of this deputy premiership and no end was found; the Cabinet effective 5 January 2018, which names him Minister of Lands only, supplies none. His acting premiership from 1 September 2017 is a claim on to_pm. A separate observation from his 2020-2021 deputy premiership.

holder_claims.name: Semisi Kioa Lafu Sika
holder_claims.note: Appointed Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Infrastructure and Tourism with effect from 5 January 2018; attested to 8 November 2018 (TO-DPM-08).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end is stated: the Assembly's retrospective 'Sanuali 2018 - Sepitema 2019' gives months only, and no end is inferred from Fa'otusia's appointment of 9 October 2019. holder_claims.name: Sione Vuna Fa'otusia
holder_claims.note: Appointed Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Justice and Prison with effect from 9 October 2019; styled Deputy Prime Minister on 16 April 2020 (TO-DPM-09). Sworn in the Assembly on 28 October 2019 as 'Hon. Vuna Fa'otusia'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The oath is a separate claim and not a start. His resignation is known only as 'in 2020' (Assembly, retrospective) and 'Okatopa 2019 - 2020' (Assembly list), so no until is set.

holder_claims.name: Lord Ma'afu
holder_claims.note: Deputy Prime Minister on the Assembly's member page as captured on 21 April 2021 and styled so by the PMO at his death in Auckland in the early hours of Sunday 12 December 2021 (TO-DPM-10).
holder_claims.uncertainty: The start is known only as 'mei Tisema 2020' (Assembly list, month only), so the holder is event-dated to the capture; until is the stated day of his death in office. holder_claims.name: Poasi Mataele Tei
holder_claims.note: Appointed Deputy Prime Minister, with MEIDECC and Public Enterprises, with effect from 28 December 2021 (TO-TR21-06).
holder_claims.uncertainty: The start is the stated effective date of the ministerial appointments. The letter of appointment was presented and the oath taken on 29 December, recorded as a separate claim. No end date or term is inferred.

holder_claims.name: Samiu Vaipulu
holder_claims.note: Printed as 'Hon. Samiu Vaipulu', Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Justice and Prisons, in the members' list of the minutes of 9 December 2024 (TO-TR24-02). The Assembly's 24 December 2024 roll and the PMO's 6 January 2025 announcement print 'Samiu Kuita Vaipulu'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: A dated membership-list observation only; his appointment date and the end of his deputy premiership are unrecorded, and Poasi Mataele Tei's 2021 observation gains no end from it. holder_claims.name: Taniela Likuohihifo Fusimalohi

holder_claims.uncertainty: The start is the stated effective date of the ministerial appointments. The letters of appointment were forecast for 30 January (unconfirmed) and the oath was taken in the Assembly on 31 January; both are separate claims. No end date or term is inferred.

roles.title: Speaker

holder_claims.name: Fusitu'a
holder_claims.note: Court records attest him as Speaker: the Court of Appeal quotes the Speaker's committal warrant of 20 September 1996, signed 'Fusitu'a / Chairman of the Legislative Assembly', and the Supreme Court found that when he was interviewed as the Speaker on 14 November 1996 he was 'at all material times the Speaker'. Event-dated to 14 November 1996, the day of that explicit finding.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No appointment instrument, start or end was found. His appointment year is 1990, 1991 or 1995 in the Assembly's retrospectives (to_la_list_fusitua_1990_1998_20111130, to_la_obituary_fusitua_appointed_1991_20140505, to_la_archives_fusitua_1995_1998_20060327); none is a boundary, and the lists' 1998 end is not used. The courts name him only by his noble title.

holder_claims.name: Hon. Veikune
holder_claims.note: First term. The government's Legislative Assembly page presented him as Speaker when captured on 30 April 2001 (last modified 19 February 2001) and in its revision of 14 December 2001.
holder_claims.uncertainty: Event-dated to the first capture only; the roster could lag (a capture of August 2002, after his successor's appointment had been reported, still marked him Speaker). His appointment (1998 or 1999 in the Assembly's retrospectives) and the end of this term (2001 or 2002) are unresolved; no end is inferred from Tu'ivakano's 2002 appointment, which the government statement says 'succeeds the Hon. Veikune'.

holder_claims.name: Hon. Tu'ivakano
holder_claims.note: Presented as Speaker by the government's Legislative Assembly page (revision of 8 April 2003), the Assembly's home page (captured 6 September 2004) and the government page's revision of 19 September 2004 (captured 26 December 2004).
holder_claims.uncertainty: Event-dated to the earliest attestation after the two conflicting appointment dates, 'last week' in a statement of about 23 May 2002 (to_speaker_tuivakano_appointment_reported_20020523) and 1 July 2002 in the Assembly's later statements; neither is a start. No end is stated: he was replaced by Veikune's appointment of 22 March 2005 after becoming Minister of Works, but no source gives the day his Speakership ended, and none is inferred.

holder_claims.name: Hon. Veikune
holder_claims.note: Second term. The Assembly's Speaker page says King Taufa'ahau Tupou IV appointed him on 22 March 2005 (an appointment day, not a stated effective day, so no from). The PMO release of 9 February 2006 states that his position as Speaker ended on 25 January 2006, as the Acting Private Secretary to His Majesty confirmed on 3 February 2006.
holder_claims.uncertainty: until is the stated end day. The appointment instrument was not seen, and IPU's 23 March 2005 statement is corroboration only. The Land Court's 2007 recital of his removal (to_speaker_veikune_removal_recited_20071213) gives no day and is not used.

holder_claims.name: Lord Tu'ilakepa
holder_claims.note: Signed the Assembly's reply of 2 June 2008 to the Princess Regent's Speech from the Throne as 'Sea 'o e Fale Alea', and presided as Speaker on 29 June 2010 in a government-published transcript that addresses a petition to 'Lord Tu'ilakepa, 'Eiki Sea 'o e Fale Alea'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: Event-dated to the reply, which prints only 'Tu'ilakepa'. No appointment instrument or release was found; the day 2 May 2008 appears only in IPU's 2008 summary, which the Crown packet holds and this holder does not cite. No end is stated, and the Interim Speaker of December 2010 (to_interim_speaker_tupou_styled_20101203) is not used as one.

holder_claims.name: Lord Lasike
holder_claims.note: Selected unopposed by the Assembly on 21 December 2010, with the royal appointment then still to come (claims, not a start). Event-dated to 14 January 2011, the first dated record of him acting as Speaker. The end is the King's revocation of his appointment under clause 61(2)(c), stated as effective immediately and conveyed by letter on 17 July 2012.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The royal appointment day is unknown, so from stays null. until rests on the release's 'effective immediately' and the letter dated 17 July 2012; the instrument's own date is not printed. The conviction of 9 July 2012 and the loss of his seat are not used as the end. No identity is asserted with 'the Honourable Lasike' who acted as Speaker in 1995.

holder_claims.name: Lord Fakafanua
holder_claims.note: Elected 17-8 by the Assembly on 19 July 2012; the Assembly's item of 23 July dates his royal appointment to that day and its item of 20 July reports the appointment as done. He began presiding on 23 July 2012 and is attested as Speaker to 14 August 2014.
holder_claims.uncertainty: An appointment day with no stated effective date, so it is event-dated through attested_on, as the prime-minister holders of CLAUDE-C01-08 are. The Assembly's Tongan item created at 17:23 on 19 July still called the appointment pending (to_fakafanua_royal_appointment_pending_20120719); the conservative alternative is 20 July 2012, when it was reported as done. 'Started in his new role ... this morning' (23 July) is not taken as from, because the same item dates the appointment earlier. No end is stated, and nothing is inferred from the 2014 election or from clause 61(2)(a).

holder_claims.name: Lord Tu'ivakano
holder_claims.note: Styled Lord Speaker by the Assembly's news item of 24 February 2015. His election by the House on 29 December 2014 is recorded in the prime-minister packet (to_pohiva_declared_pm_elect_pmo_20141229), which this holder does not cite.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No royal appointment or oath for this Assembly is dated by any source retrieved, so no start is stated. No end is stated either: the Speaker's release of 12 September 2017 already in the packet still names him Speaker. The Assembly's profile identifies him with the Hon. Tu'ivakano who was Speaker in 2002-2005, but that identity is not needed for this observation.

holder_claims.name: Lord Fakafanua
holder_claims.note: Styled Speaker, addressing the first sitting held at the Tonga National Centre, in the Assembly's item of 5 March 2018. He took the oath as 'the Lord Speaker Fakafanua' on 18 January 2018 (to_speaker_fakafanua_sworn_news_20180118; the oath is not a start), and the Assembly's election of 18 December 2017 is recorded in the prime-minister packet (to_pohiva_assembly_reselection_20171218).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No royal appointment for this Assembly is dated, so there is no start; no end is stated. This is a separate holder observation from the 2012-2014 one, and no continuity or gap between the two is asserted.

holder_claims.name: Lord Fakafanua
holder_claims.note: Styled Speaker in the Assembly's item of 17 February 2022, after the Assembly's election of December 2021 (to_speaker_fakafanua_assembly_election_20211215). Claims of the 2024-2025 transition packet style him Speaker on 9 and 10 December 2024 and 31 January 2025 (to_palace_acceptance_letter_20241209, to_pm_nominations_invited_20241210, to_eke_oath_20250131); this holder does not cite them.
holder_claims.uncertainty: A separate holder observation for the Assembly elected in November 2021: no continuity with, or gap after, the 2017-2021 holder is asserted. No royal appointment for this Assembly is dated, so there is no start. No end is stated: 'Former Speaker' (16 December 2025) and Lord Vaea's succession (19 December 2025) are not end dates.

holder_claims.name: Lord Vaea
holder_claims.note: The latest official styling found before the cutoff: the Assembly's press release of 19 May 2026 says the delegation to China was led by the Speaker, Lord Vaea. His royal appointment effective 18 December 2025 is the existing string holder to_speakers_appointment, which stays first and unchanged; the Assembly's election (item of 16 December 2025) and his oath (22 January 2026) are separate claims.
holder_claims.uncertainty: An attestation, not a term: no from or until. The Acting Speaker presiding on 18 August 2026 (to_acting_speaker_tuihaangana_20260818) is a claim only and neither names nor ends his Speakership.

roles.scope_note: Holder observations carry from/until only where a source states the day: a stated end of office, or a revocation stated as effective immediately. A royal appointment dated without a stated effective day, and an in-office attestation (a roster, a signature, a presiding record or a styling), are event-dated through attested_on. The Assembly's election or recommendation of its Speaker and its report to the King, oaths, resignation announcements, acting and interim Speakers, a Deputy Speaker presiding, retrospective lists and statute or constitution texts are claims, never holders or boundaries. The 2025 royal appointment remains the string observation to_speakers_appointment (CLAUDE-C01-24).
